scope: Adversarial test-only gameplan review. No browser run, production modification, runtime proof, or acceptance closure.

findings.problem: The fallback permits PASS without showing that the changed reference reached the actual DOM. This is unnecessary for the pinned fixture: checker.reference assigns signature_ref the target signature ID as its nominal type; model.typeLabel resolves that ID to A or B; ExpressionEditor Branch renders that type in the real block button. Generation plus 500 buttons could pass an implementation with stale block labels.
findings.required_fix: Require each edited block button to display the independently expected A/B nominal type, with its exact fixture node ID, after the matching commit and frames. Require the opposite pre-edit target and expected post-edit target in committed state. Missing or mismatched target-specific DOM evidence makes the series INCOMPLETE; do not substitute a caveat and PASS. No fake labels or production edits are needed.

findings.problem: The protocol does not define freshness and identity of the matching React commit sufficiently to prevent stale notifications, controller-ref observations, or another draft with the same generation from ending the interval. publish synchronously updates controller.current before React commits.
findings.required_fix: Specify a commit-phase marker from the rendered Workbench view (for example a layout effect), arm it before dispatch, and match a fresh commit to workbench mount identity, documentId, baseRevision, draftId and exactly previous contentGeneration + 1. Schedule the first rAF only after that commit and the second only inside the first; end with a fresh monotonic performance.now read in callback two, rather than reusing the rAF frame timestamp. Reject unmount, missing commit, identity/content replacement and timeout as INCOMPLETE. Preserve ordinary advisory behavior and evidence.

refinements: Pin and report initial and post-edit unique owned-node ID sets, not just button counts. Check all 1100 edits alter exactly one signature_ref target with no ID/count changes, and check depth and source bound before mounting. Exact fixture/file and compact edit hashes currently match; inspected file has 500 nodes, 1100 edits and 2565 UTF-8 source bytes.

Explicitly use nearest-rank measured indexes 499, 949 and 989 after numeric sorting of 1000 finite nonnegative millisecond samples. Apply strict p95 < 50 to unrounded values; displayed rounding must not affect classification. Preserve failed runs and invalidation evidence.

Record foreground/visibility transitions and callback timeouts. Do not erase slow samples or rerun only unfavorable events; uninterrupted valid slow runs remain FAIL. Record worker startup included/excluded as requested by spec even though this browser-only interval excludes authoritative diagnostic startup.

Lean classify is count-and-external-threshold classification only: it neither derives p95 from samples nor models validity. Its constructed ordering trace has one frameOpportunity abstract event, not evidence of two runtime callbacks. Keep that abstraction explicit; any formal-build success cannot certify runtime correspondence or visual correctness.
accepted_boundaries: Actual AllowApp and accepted-document setup are feasible; DocumentBody mounts only when accepted is present. Test-only source transform must be exact and fail closed.

100 warmups then 1000 sequential actual changeModule edits, real React commit plus two rAF callbacks, strict warm p95 < 50 ms is a defensible declared preview interval once the blocking validity rules are tightened.
No physical paint, server diagnostics, solver, manual assistive-technology, commercial-rights or market acceptance claims follow from this benchmark.
